avertissement: Traduction anglaise préparée par l'équipe avec l'aide d'une IA, à relire. Le français fait foi.

textes.sextorsion.m1-1: Hi! I came across your profile, you have a really lovely smile.
textes.sextorsion.m1-3: You seem really interesting. Want to chat?
textes.sextorsion.o1-1: Kevin answers right away, piles on the compliments and already asks about your private life.
textes.sextorsion.a1-1: Chatting is not a mistake. Just notice how fast he tries to get close.
textes.sextorsion.o1-2: Kevin dodges: “Not yet, but I feel like I've known you forever.” He says nothing specific about himself.
textes.sextorsion.a1-2: Asking a question is a good reflex: a vague answer is already a clue.
textes.sextorsion.o1-3: You leave the message unanswered. Kevin writes again twice that evening.
textes.sextorsion.a1-3: You never have to answer. A stranger who keeps insisting is a signal worth noting.
textes.sextorsion.f1: A flattering approach can be sincere, but it can also be a way to win your trust quickly. Take time to observe.
textes.sextorsion.m2-1: I really think we could be close.
textes.sextorsion.m2-2: If you like me, send me a private photo. You can trust me.
textes.sextorsion.o2-1: In the story, the photo is sent. Kevin says thanks… and keeps the picture. There is no way to take it back.
textes.sextorsion.a2-1: If this happens to you, it is not your fault: he is the one abusing your trust. You have the right to change your mind and ask for help at any time.
textes.sextorsion.o2-2: Kevin insists: “Don't you trust me?”, then turns cold. His reaction shows that your limit bothers him.
textes.sextorsion.a2-2: Saying no is enough. Someone who respects you accepts your refusal without making you feel guilty.
textes.sextorsion.o2-3: Kevin answers: “To prove you care about me.” He gives no real reason, only pressure.
textes.sextorsion.a2-3: Asking questions helps you see the manipulation: affection is never proven with an intimate picture.
textes.sextorsion.f2: Your consent must be free, informed and reversible. Trust is never proven by sending an intimate image.
textes.sextorsion.m3-1: Look what's been going around since this morning!
textes.sextorsion.m3-2: Hidden image · humiliating content about a young girl
textes.sextorsion.o3-1: Within minutes the image reaches other groups. Nobody can stop it anymore, and the girl is even more exposed.
textes.sextorsion.a3-1: You can still act: stop forwarding it, delete it and report it to the platform.
textes.sextorsion.o3-2: Your reaction adds to the others: the message rises in the group and the image stays visible longer.
textes.sextorsion.a3-2: Even an emoji keeps the message alive. Better not to react, to report it, and to write to the victim privately.
textes.sextorsion.o3-3: You write in the group that sharing this is violence, then you send a message of support to the girl. Two friends delete the image.
textes.sextorsion.a3-3: Refusing to share and supporting the victim is what slows the spread.
textes.sextorsion.f3: Sharing an intimate image without consent adds to the violence. Even if you didn't create it, you can choose not to pass it on.
textes.sextorsion.m4-2: If you don't do what I say, I'll post everything.
textes.sextorsion.m4-3: You have until tonight to send me the money.
textes.sextorsion.o4-1: Kevin takes the money… then asks for a bigger amount the next day. The threat doesn't stop.
textes.sextorsion.a4-1: Paying never guarantees that blackmail stops. You can always stop paying, keep the evidence and ask for help.
textes.sextorsion.o4-2: Kevin answers with new threats and things escalate. Every reply gives him more to work with.
textes.sextorsion.a4-2: Your anger is legitimate. The most protective thing is still to stop answering, keep the evidence and block the account.
textes.sextorsion.c4-3: Keep the evidence and ask for help
textes.sextorsion.o4-3: You take screenshots, block Kevin and talk to someone you trust. You are no longer alone against him.
textes.sextorsion.a4-3: This is the most protective reflex: evidence, blocking, reporting, support.
textes.sextorsion.f4: You are not responsible for the threat. Paying doesn't guarantee it stops. Keep the evidence without putting yourself in danger, block the account and look for support.
textes.faux-recrutement.m1-1: Hello, we are hiring hostesses for a big hotel. Salary: 300,000 F a month.
textes.faux-recrutement.m1-2: No diploma needed, just a good appearance. Answer quickly, only two places left.
textes.faux-recrutement.c1-1: Answer right away and give my details
textes.faux-recrutement.o1-1: Mrs Dossou congratulates you and asks for your address and age, without saying anything about the company.
textes.faux-recrutement.a1-1: Wanting to work is legitimate. Before giving your details, check who is contacting you.
textes.faux-recrutement.c1-2: Look up the agency and the hotel
textes.faux-recrutement.o1-2: You find no address, no website, no reviews. The hotel has posted no job offer.
textes.faux-recrutement.a1-2: A real company leaves traces you can check. No traces at all is a warning sign.
textes.faux-recrutement.c1-3: Show the offer to someone I trust
textes.faux-recrutement.o1-3: Your cousin frowns: “A salary like that, with no diploma and no interview? Be careful.”
textes.faux-recrutement.a1-3: A second opinion helps you see what excitement can hide.
textes.faux-recrutement.f1: An offer that is too good, urgent and focused on appearance should alert you. Always check who is hiring.
textes.faux-recrutement.m2-1: For your file, send three full-length photos of yourself in tight clothes.
textes.faux-recrutement.m2-2: The client chooses the girls from photos. That's normal in the hotel business.
textes.faux-recrutement.c2-1: Send the photos so I don't miss the job
textes.faux-recrutement.o2-1: She replies: “Perfect, the client is interested.” Your photos are now in the hands of strangers.
textes.faux-recrutement.a2-1: You wanted to seize a chance, that's not a mistake. Keep the conversation: it proves what you were asked for.
textes.faux-recrutement.c2-2: Refuse: nobody gets hired on their looks
textes.faux-recrutement.o2-2: She insists: “Otherwise your application is lost.” The pressure confirms the trap.
textes.faux-recrutement.a2-2: A serious employer judges your skills, not your body. You have the right to say no.
textes.faux-recrutement.o2-3: You keep the account name, the messages and the date.
textes.faux-recrutement.a2-3: These screenshots can help if you report the account or file a complaint.
textes.faux-recrutement.f2: Asking for photos of your body for a job is not normal. It is often the way into exploitation.
textes.faux-recrutement.m3-1: Fill in your application here, with your ID.
textes.faux-recrutement.m4-1: Your interview is tonight at 9 pm, room 12. Come alone.
textes.faux-recrutement.m4-2: Don't tell anyone, other girls are waiting to take your place.
textes.faux-recrutement.c4-1: Go alone so I don't lose the job
textes.faux-recrutement.o4-1: In the taxi you hesitate and text your cousin. She begs you to turn back.
textes.faux-recrutement.a4-1: You did nothing wrong by hoping for this job. But an interview alone, at night, in a hotel room, puts you in danger.
textes.faux-recrutement.c4-2: Refuse: interviews happen in an office, during the day
textes.faux-recrutement.o4-2: She offers no office. She just repeats: “Tonight or never.”
textes.faux-recrutement.a4-2: A real recruiter accepts a daytime meeting, in a public or professional place.
textes.faux-recrutement.c4-3: Show everything to someone close and keep the evidence
textes.faux-recrutement.o4-3: Your aunt reads the messages and goes with you to report the account.
textes.faux-recrutement.a4-3: “Don't tell anyone” is a sign of a trap. Talking about it protects you.
textes.faux-recrutement.f4: Secrecy, urgency, night-time and a hotel: together, these are the signs of a trap that can lead to exploitation.
textes.faux-recrutement.m5-1: You made us lose a client. We have your photos and your address.
textes.faux-recrutement.m5-2: Come tomorrow, or your photos will go around with your name.
textes.faux-recrutement.c5-1: Give in and go so it stops
textes.faux-recrutement.o5-1: Giving in guarantees nothing: the threat can start again and put you in danger.
textes.faux-recrutement.a5-1: Your fear is normal. You can still stop and ask for help at any time.
textes.faux-recrutement.c5-2: Block, keep the evidence and file a complaint
textes.faux-recrutement.o5-2: With your screenshots, you file a complaint, with someone by your side. The account is reported.
textes.faux-recrutement.a5-2: Threatening to share photos is punished by law. Filing a complaint is free.
textes.faux-recrutement.c5-3: Call the National Institute for Women
textes.faux-recrutement.o5-3: At 114, a counsellor listens to you, explains your rights and tells you where to go.
textes.faux-recrutement.a5-3: You don't have to face this alone. Free services exist to support you.
textes.faux-recrutement.f5: Fake job offers are sometimes used to trap women. Don't give in: keep the evidence and get support.
textes.compte-pirate.m1-1: Hi darling, it's Chantal! I changed my number, save this one.
textes.compte-pirate.m1-2: How are you? I need a small favour.
textes.compte-pirate.o1-1: “Chantal” thanks you warmly and goes straight to her request, without asking how you are.
textes.compte-pirate.a1-1: Wanting to help a friend is a good quality. Just notice that nothing proves yet that it's really her.
textes.compte-pirate.c1-2: I'll call your old number to check
textes.compte-pirate.o1-2: “No no, it doesn't work anymore, write to me here.” She avoids the call.
textes.compte-pirate.a1-2: Checking through another channel than the chat is the right reflex. A refusal is already a clue.
textes.compte-pirate.c1-3: Send me a voice message so I recognise your voice
textes.compte-pirate.o1-3: “My mic is broken.” Always an excuse, never any proof.
textes.compte-pirate.a1-3: Asking for simple proof, like a voice, helps spot someone pretending to be someone else.
textes.compte-pirate.f1: “I changed my number” is a common way to pose as someone close to you. Always check with a call or in person.
textes.compte-pirate.m2-1: I sent you a 6-digit code by mistake, it was meant for me.
textes.compte-pirate.m2-2: Please send it back to me quickly, it's urgent!
textes.compte-pirate.o2-1: A few minutes later you are logged out of your messaging app. The code was used to open your account on another phone.
textes.compte-pirate.a2-1: It's not your fault: the request came with a friend's name. If this happens, log back in quickly with your number and turn on two-step verification.
textes.compte-pirate.c2-2: Ask why the code came to me
textes.compte-pirate.o2-2: “It's a network error, hurry up and send it!” No explanation, only rushing.
textes.compte-pirate.a2-2: A code arrives on your phone because it concerns your account, not someone else's.
textes.compte-pirate.o2-3: “Chantal” insists, then gets angry. You don't give in, and your account stays yours.
textes.compte-pirate.a2-3: A code received by SMS is never shared, not even with someone close.
textes.compte-pirate.f2: A verification code is the key to your account. Whoever gets it can read your messages and write to your contacts as you.
textes.compte-pirate.m3-1: OK, otherwise click here to confirm it's really your account.
textes.compte-pirate.m4-1: Are you the one sending embarrassing messages to the group's customers? That's not like you.
textes.compte-pirate.m4-2: Your account is offering dates to men in your name.
textes.compte-pirate.o4-1: The messages keep going out in your name. Customers start talking about you.
textes.compte-pirate.a4-1: The shame belongs to the person impersonating you, not to you. Speaking up quickly limits the damage.
textes.compte-pirate.c4-2: Warn the group: my account was hacked
textes.compte-pirate.o4-2: You write from Awa's phone: “It's not me.” The group stops answering the fake account.
textes.compte-pirate.a4-2: Warning your contacts protects your reputation and cuts off the manipulation.
textes.compte-pirate.c4-3: Get my account back and turn on two-step verification
textes.compte-pirate.o4-3: You log back in with your number, change your password and turn on two-step verification.
textes.compte-pirate.a4-3: Two-step verification stops someone from taking your account back with a simple code.
textes.compte-pirate.f4: Whoever takes your account can make you say anything. Warn your contacts and secure your account.
textes.compte-pirate.m5-1: I had time to read your conversations and see your private photos.
textes.compte-pirate.m5-2: Send me more, or I'll post everything on your sales page.
textes.compte-pirate.c5-1: Send what he asks so he keeps quiet
textes.compte-pirate.o5-1: He asks for more the next day. Every time you send something, he gets more power.
textes.compte-pirate.a5-1: It's not your fault: you were trapped. You can stop at any time and ask for help.
textes.compte-pirate.c5-2: Stop answering, keep the evidence and file a complaint
textes.compte-pirate.o5-2: You take screenshots and file a complaint. The National Centre for Digital Investigations handles these cases.
textes.compte-pirate.a5-2: Blackmail with intimate images is punished by law. Keep everything before you block.
textes.compte-pirate.c5-3: Warn my customers and get the page blocked
textes.compte-pirate.o5-3: You post that your account was hacked and report the page. Your customers support you.
textes.compte-pirate.a5-3: Speaking up first takes the blackmailer's weapon away.
textes.compte-pirate.f5: A hacked account can become a tool for blackmail. Don't give in: evidence, complaint, support.
textes.controle-couple.m1-1: Babe, give me your phone code. There shouldn't be any secrets between us.
textes.controle-couple.m1-2: If you say no, it means you're hiding something from me.
textes.controle-couple.o1-1: That same evening he reads your conversations and blames you for a message from a classmate.
textes.controle-couple.a1-1: It's not your fault if he takes advantage. You can change your code at any time: it belongs to you.
textes.controle-couple.c1-2: Tell him my phone stays mine
textes.controle-couple.o1-2: He sulks, then insists. You stay calm: having your own space is not cheating.
textes.controle-couple.a1-2: Keeping your code to yourself is a right, not a betrayal.
textes.controle-couple.c1-3: Ask him why he needs it
textes.controle-couple.o1-3: He answers: “To be sure of you.” The trust he demands comes through watching you.
textes.controle-couple.a1-3: Asking questions lets you see the control behind the words of love.
textes.controle-couple.f1: In a healthy relationship, each person keeps their own codes and private life. Demanding your phone is a form of control.
textes.controle-couple.m2-1: Turn on location sharing. That way I always know where you are, it's for your safety.
textes.controle-couple.c2-1: Turn it on to keep the peace
textes.controle-couple.o2-1: He asks why you were at a friend's place instead of going home. Every outing becomes a fight.
textes.controle-couple.a2-1: You can stop sharing whenever you want. Your safety does not depend on him watching you.
textes.controle-couple.c2-2: Refuse and offer to let him know when I get home
textes.controle-couple.o2-2: He says it's not enough, but you stay in charge of where you go and with whom.
textes.controle-couple.a2-2: Letting him know when you decide to is your choice. Being followed all the time is not.
textes.controle-couple.c2-3: Talk about it with a friend I trust
textes.controle-couple.o2-3: Your friend tells you her ex did the same. You feel less alone in seeing things clearly.
textes.controle-couple.a2-3: Talking about it helps you recognise control, which often creeps in little by little.
textes.controle-couple.f2: Tracking someone's location all the time, even “out of love”, is surveillance.
textes.controle-couple.m3-1: Install this app, it's so we can be closer. Click, it's quick.
textes.controle-couple.m4-1: How do you know what I told my sister yesterday?
textes.controle-couple.m4-2: I know everything, don't bother. You have nothing to hide from me.
textes.controle-couple.o4-1: He keeps reading your conversations. You start keeping quiet with everyone.
textes.controle-couple.a4-1: It's not up to you to stay silent. There is help to check your phone and protect yourself.
textes.controle-couple.c4-2: Check my apps and change my passwords
textes.controle-couple.o4-2: You find an unknown app, write down its name, then change your passwords from a safe phone.
textes.controle-couple.a4-2: Write down what you find before deleting it: it can be used as evidence. If you fear his reaction, ask for advice first.
textes.controle-couple.c4-3: Ask a support service for advice
textes.controle-couple.o4-3: They explain how to check your phone without making him angry, and how to protect yourself.
textes.controle-couple.a4-3: When the surveillance comes from someone close, acting with support is safer.
textes.controle-couple.f4: A spy app installed by someone close is violence. It's not your fault and you can get help.
textes.controle-couple.m5-1: If you leave me, I'll send our conversations to your whole family.
textes.controle-couple.m5-2: You know I have everything on my phone.
textes.controle-couple.o5-1: The threats come back with every disagreement. Fear decides for you.
textes.controle-couple.a5-1: Giving in doesn't stop blackmail. You have the right to leave and to be protected.
textes.controle-couple.c5-2: Beg him not to do anything
textes.controle-couple.o5-2: He sees that the threat works and uses it again the next day.
textes.controle-couple.a5-2: You don't have to negotiate with a threat. Keep the messages and look for support.
textes.controle-couple.o5-3: You take dated screenshots and call the INF. They listen and explain your rights.
textes.controle-couple.a5-3: Threatening to share private conversations is punished by law. You are not alone.
textes.controle-couple.f5: Blackmail to stop you from leaving is violence. The law protects you: keep the evidence and ask for help.
textes.faux-profil.m1-1: Is that you, this new account with your photo? It's asking everyone for money.
textes.faux-profil.m1-2: It already wrote to your aunt.
textes.faux-profil.o1-1: The fake account keeps going and two people send money thinking they're helping you.
textes.faux-profil.a1-1: Acting fast limits the damage, and you are not the one to blame.
textes.faux-profil.c1-2: Report the account and warn my contacts
textes.faux-profil.o1-2: You post: “This account is not me, don't answer it.” Rachida and others report it too.
textes.faux-profil.a1-2: Reporting and warning people protects those close to you. Several reports get the account removed faster.
textes.faux-profil.c1-3: Take screenshots of the fake account
textes.faux-profil.o1-3: You keep its name, its link and its messages, with the date.
textes.faux-profil.a1-3: These screenshots prove the impersonation if you file a complaint.
textes.faux-profil.f1: Pretending to be someone else online is an offence. Report it, warn the people close to you and keep evidence.
textes.faux-profil.m2-1: Look at the photo this account just posted 😂
textes.faux-profil.m2-2: Hidden image · edit pasting a student's face onto someone else's photo
textes.faux-profil.o2-1: Your message pushes the photo back up. It spreads to other classes.
textes.faux-profil.a2-1: Even if you didn't create it, sharing or laughing makes the violence grow.
textes.faux-profil.c2-2: Say it's fake and ask for it to be deleted
textes.faux-profil.o2-2: Two students delete the photo. Kader goes quiet.
textes.faux-profil.a2-2: Saying it's fake breaks the effect of the edit. Your support matters.
textes.faux-profil.c2-3: Write to the victim to support her
textes.faux-profil.o2-3: She replies: “Thank you, I felt so alone.” You go together to see a teacher.
textes.faux-profil.a2-3: Supporting the person targeted is one of the most useful things you can do.
textes.faux-profil.f2: A faked image humiliates even when everyone knows it's fake. Don't share it, and support the victim.
textes.faux-profil.m3-1: We blocked the fake account. Confirm your identity here to get yours back.
textes.faux-profil.m4-1: Everyone says it's really her in the photo.
textes.faux-profil.o4-1: Your replies attract even more comments. You spend the night defending yourself.
textes.faux-profil.a4-1: Justifying yourself is exhausting. You have nothing to prove.
textes.faux-profil.c4-2: Leave the group and block the authors
textes.faux-profil.o4-2: You can breathe again. A friend keeps an eye on the group and notes what is said.
textes.faux-profil.a4-2: Protecting yourself is not running away. Someone you trust can keep watch for you.
textes.faux-profil.c4-3: Show the messages to an adult I trust
textes.faux-profil.o4-3: Your aunt goes with you to see the head teacher, screenshots in hand.
textes.faux-profil.a4-3: With evidence, the school and the authorities can act.
textes.faux-profil.f4: Blaming the victim is part of the harassment. She is never the one responsible.
textes.faux-profil.m5-1: I have other edits of you. Send 20,000 F or I'll post them everywhere.
textes.faux-profil.o5-1: He asks for more the next day. The edits stay in his hands.
textes.faux-profil.a5-1: Paying doesn't stop blackmail. You can stop at any time and ask for help.
textes.faux-profil.c5-2: Tell him I'm going to file a complaint
textes.faux-profil.o5-2: He switches accounts and starts again somewhere else. Answering him gives him attention.
textes.faux-profil.a5-2: Better not to answer at all, keep the evidence and act with support.
textes.faux-profil.c5-3: Keep the evidence, report and file a complaint
textes.faux-profil.o5-3: You keep everything, report the accounts and file a complaint with your aunt. You are no longer alone.
textes.faux-profil.a5-3: Blackmail and faked images are punished by law. Filing a complaint is free.
textes.faux-profil.f5: A faked image is still violence, even if it's fake. Don't pay, keep the evidence and get support.
textes.harcelement-meute.m1-1: You sell wax prints? With that face?
textes.harcelement-meute.o1-1: Your reply gets shared and the mockery doubles.
textes.harcelement-meute.a1-1: Answering feeds the attacks. It's not up to you to silence them alone.
textes.harcelement-meute.o1-2: The comments disappear from your video. Your customers no longer see the insults.
textes.harcelement-meute.a1-2: Hiding and blocking protects your space without joining the fight.
textes.harcelement-meute.o1-3: You keep the names, the messages and the date.
textes.harcelement-meute.a1-3: Screenshots prove the attacks are repeated if they continue.
textes.harcelement-meute.f1: Insulting a woman because she is a woman is not humour.
textes.harcelement-meute.m2-1: Share her video, we'll have a good laugh.
textes.harcelement-meute.m2-2: She deserves to be taught a lesson.
textes.harcelement-meute.o2-1: Your shop disappears along with your customers. The harassers just carry on elsewhere.
textes.harcelement-meute.a2-1: You don't have to disappear. There are settings to protect you without losing everything.
textes.harcelement-meute.o2-2: Only your followers can comment. The flood stops at once.
textes.harcelement-meute.a2-2: That's exactly what privacy settings are for.
textes.harcelement-meute.c2-3: Ask friends to report with me
textes.harcelement-meute.o2-3: Several reports get the worst messages removed within a day.
textes.harcelement-meute.a2-3: Together, you carry more weight. You don't have to handle this alone.
textes.harcelement-meute.f2: When attacks come from a group, reporting together and limiting comments breaks up the pack.
textes.harcelement-meute.m3-1: Your account will be closed for abusive reports. Log in here to appeal.
textes.harcelement-meute.m4-1: Here's where she lives: the neighbourhood, the street, the blue house.
textes.harcelement-meute.c4-1: Wait for it to calm down
textes.harcelement-meute.o4-1: Others share the address. You're afraid to go out.
textes.harcelement-meute.a4-1: Posting your address so people come to see you is serious. Don't wait to protect yourself.
textes.harcelement-meute.c4-2: Warn the people close to me and not stay alone
textes.harcelement-meute.o4-2: Your cousin comes to sleep at your place and your big brother keeps an eye on the street.
textes.harcelement-meute.a4-2: Your physical safety comes first. Surround yourself with people.
textes.harcelement-meute.c4-3: Report it and go to the police
textes.harcelement-meute.o4-3: You report the post and go to the police station with your screenshots.
textes.harcelement-meute.a4-3: Sharing someone's address to expose them is an offence. If you are in immediate danger, call 117.
textes.harcelement-meute.f4: Posting a person's address to expose them puts them in real danger. Protect yourself first, then report.
textes.harcelement-meute.m5-1: We know where to find you.
textes.harcelement-meute.m5-2: Close your shop or we're coming.
textes.harcelement-meute.o5-1: You lose your income and the fear stays. The threats don't stop.
textes.harcelement-meute.a5-1: Giving in guarantees nothing. You have the right to work in safety.
textes.harcelement-meute.o5-2: Your message is used against you to say you are provoking them.
textes.harcelement-meute.a5-2: Your anger is legitimate. The safest thing is still not to answer and to keep the evidence.
textes.harcelement-meute.c5-3: Keep the evidence and file a complaint
textes.harcelement-meute.o5-3: With your screenshots, the complaint is recorded. The INF supports you, at 114.
textes.harcelement-meute.a5-3: Online threats are punished by law. You have the right to be protected.
textes.harcelement-meute.f5: An online threat is a real threat. Keep everything, file a complaint and don't stay alone.
textes.chantage-ex.m1-1: I miss you. Come back, let's forget everything.
textes.chantage-ex.m1-2: I won't accept you leaving like this.
textes.chantage-ex.c1-1: Explain at length why I'm leaving
textes.chantage-ex.o1-1: He argues with every sentence. The discussion lasts all night and you feel guilty.
textes.chantage-ex.a1-1: You don't have to justify leaving. A clear decision is enough.
textes.chantage-ex.c1-2: Tell him calmly that it's over
textes.chantage-ex.o1-2: “It's over, I wish you the best.” You put your phone down.
textes.chantage-ex.a1-2: A short, firm message avoids opening a negotiation.
textes.chantage-ex.c1-3: Talk to a friend about it
textes.chantage-ex.o1-3: Your best friend calls you back: “You have the right to leave. I'm here.”
textes.chantage-ex.a1-3: Not facing a difficult break-up alone protects you.
textes.chantage-ex.f1: Leaving is a right. Nobody can force you to stay, face to face or online.
textes.chantage-ex.m2-1: Remember the photo you sent me? It's still on my phone.
textes.chantage-ex.m2-2: It would be a shame if your family saw it.
textes.chantage-ex.o2-1: He answers: “That depends on you.” Your begging shows him he has power.
textes.chantage-ex.a2-1: Your fear is understandable. Better to keep his messages than to answer him.
textes.chantage-ex.o2-2: You keep his name, his number and his messages, with the date and time.
textes.chantage-ex.a2-2: These screenshots prove the threat. They will help if you file a complaint.
textes.chantage-ex.c2-3: Show the messages to someone I trust
textes.chantage-ex.o2-3: Your big sister reads everything and tells you: “You're not the one to blame. We'll act.”
textes.chantage-ex.a2-3: Talking breaks the isolation that blackmail tries to create.
textes.chantage-ex.f2: A photo sent in trust gives no rights. Sharing it without consent is violence punished by law.
textes.chantage-ex.m3-1: Come to my place tonight. Otherwise I'll send it to the neighbourhood group.
textes.chantage-ex.o3-1: Giving in only pushes the threat back. He'll know it works.
textes.chantage-ex.a3-1: Nobody deserves to be forced. You can still ask for help at any time.
textes.chantage-ex.o3-2: You stop answering. You keep your screenshots and stay surrounded by people.
textes.chantage-ex.a3-2: Not answering anymore cuts the hold he has on you.
textes.chantage-ex.c3-3: Call the National Institute for Women
textes.chantage-ex.o3-3: At 114, they listen to you without judging and explain how to file a complaint.
textes.chantage-ex.a3-3: Free and confidential services exist to support you.
textes.chantage-ex.f3: Blackmail doesn't stop when you give in. It stops when you are surrounded and protected.
textes.chantage-ex.m4-1: I sent it. Now everyone knows who you are.
textes.chantage-ex.c4-1: Delete all my accounts and cut myself off
textes.chantage-ex.o4-1: You disappear, but the photo keeps spreading and you stay alone with your pain.
textes.chantage-ex.a4-1: What you feel is violent. Before deleting everything, keep the evidence and talk to someone.
textes.chantage-ex.c4-2: Report the post and ask for it to be removed
textes.chantage-ex.o4-2: Your friends report it too. The platform removes the image and blocks the account.
textes.chantage-ex.a4-2: Several reports get an intimate image removed faster.
textes.chantage-ex.c4-3: File a complaint with my evidence
textes.chantage-ex.o4-3: With your sister by your side, you file a complaint. Sharing an intimate image without consent is punished.
textes.chantage-ex.a4-3: Filing a complaint is free. The law protects your identity during the procedure.
textes.chantage-ex.f4: Shame must change sides: the fault lies with the person who shares, never with you.
textes.nouvel-ami.m1-1: Hi! I saw you at the school match, you're so pretty.
textes.nouvel-ami.m1-2: I'm 17. Will you give me your number?
textes.nouvel-ami.o1-1: He writes to you every evening, with lots of compliments.
textes.nouvel-ami.a1-1: Feeling flattered is normal. But your number is precious information: keep it for people you really know.
textes.nouvel-ami.c1-2: Look at his profile before answering
textes.nouvel-ami.o1-2: Blurry photo, account created a week ago, no friends in common.
textes.nouvel-ami.a1-2: A new, blurry profile with no friends in common should make you suspicious.
textes.nouvel-ami.c1-3: Ask a friend if she knows him
textes.nouvel-ami.o1-3: Nobody at school knows him, not from the match or anywhere else.
textes.nouvel-ami.a1-3: Checking with real people helps you spot a fake profile.
textes.nouvel-ami.f1: Online, only accept people you really know in real life.
textes.nouvel-ami.m2-1: Don't tell anyone we're talking. Your parents wouldn't understand.
textes.nouvel-ami.o2-1: You hide your conversations. You feel more and more alone with him.
textes.nouvel-ami.a2-1: He is trying to isolate you. You can always talk about it, even later.
textes.nouvel-ami.c2-2: Tell him I don't keep secrets with a stranger
textes.nouvel-ami.o2-2: He gets upset: “I thought you were mature.” Guilt is his tool.
textes.nouvel-ami.a2-2: A caring person never demands secrecy.
textes.nouvel-ami.c2-3: Tell my big sister about it
textes.nouvel-ami.o2-3: Your sister reads the messages: “A 17-year-old boy doesn't talk like that. Be careful.”
textes.nouvel-ami.a2-3: Talking to someone close is the best reflex as soon as you're asked to hide something.
textes.nouvel-ami.f2: “It's our secret” is a classic sign of someone manipulating a minor. Tell an adult you trust.
textes.nouvel-ami.m3-1: I bought you some phone credit! Click here to get it.
textes.nouvel-ami.m4-1: Send me a photo of you, just for me. Not your profile one.
textes.nouvel-ami.m4-2: If you really care about me, you'll do it.
textes.nouvel-ami.c4-1: Send a photo to make him happy
textes.nouvel-ami.o4-1: He immediately asks for another photo, “more personal”.
textes.nouvel-ami.a4-1: It's not your fault: he manipulated you. You can stop and tell an adult everything right now.
textes.nouvel-ami.o4-2: You block him. Your phone goes quiet again.
textes.nouvel-ami.a4-2: You have the right to say no, without explaining yourself.
textes.nouvel-ami.c4-3: Show his messages to an adult I trust
textes.nouvel-ami.o4-3: Your mother takes screenshots and calls the children's helpline.
textes.nouvel-ami.a4-3: An adult can act where you can't on your own.
textes.nouvel-ami.f4: An adult who asks a minor for photos is committing an offence. It is never the child's fault.
textes.nouvel-ami.m5-1: Actually, I'm 26. Come and see me on Saturday, alone.
textes.nouvel-ami.m5-2: Otherwise I'll tell the whole school you wrote to me.
textes.nouvel-ami.c5-1: Go alone so he keeps quiet
textes.nouvel-ami.o5-1: Meeting an adult who threatens you, alone, puts you in great danger.
textes.nouvel-ami.a5-1: You can still stop everything: call an adult or 138, even at the last minute.
textes.nouvel-ami.c5-2: Don't go and show everything to a parent
textes.nouvel-ami.o5-2: Your parents keep the evidence and go with you to the police station.
textes.nouvel-ami.a5-2: His threat has no power when adults are protecting you.
textes.nouvel-ami.o5-3: At 138, they listen to you and alert the child protection services.
textes.nouvel-ami.a5-3: 138 is free. The juvenile police unit protects child victims.
textes.nouvel-ami.f5: Approaching a minor online to manipulate her is punished by law. Speak up, keep the evidence, call 138.
textes.traque.m1-1: Nice photo in front of the campus today 😉
textes.traque.o1-1: He answers right away and comments on every one of your posts.
textes.traque.a1-1: Being polite is natural. With a stranger who keeps insisting, you don't have to answer.
textes.traque.o1-2: He can no longer see your new photos.
textes.traque.a1-2: Choosing who sees your posts is your first protection.
textes.traque.c1-3: Take a screenshot and don't answer
textes.traque.o1-3: You keep his message. He gets no answer from you.
textes.traque.a1-3: Keeping a record from the start helps if things get worse.
textes.traque.f1: By default, many posts are visible to everyone. Check your settings.
textes.traque.m2-1: You were at the market at 5 pm, right? You walk fast.
textes.traque.m2-2: Be careful, it gets dark early these days.
textes.traque.o2-1: He answers: “I know a lot of things about you.” He enjoys scaring you.
textes.traque.a2-1: Answering gives him the attention he wants. Keep his messages instead.
textes.traque.c2-2: Turn off location sharing in my apps
textes.traque.o2-2: You turn off location and the automatic sharing of your outings.
textes.traque.a2-2: A live shared location lets anyone follow you.
textes.traque.c2-3: Warn the people close to me
textes.traque.o2-3: Your flatmate decides to walk home with you in the evenings for a while.
textes.traque.a2-3: The people close to you can look out for you. You don't have to handle this alone.
textes.traque.f2: Post your outings afterwards, never live, and turn off automatic location.
textes.traque.m3-1: Look, I found you on this site. All your photos are there.
textes.traque.m4-1: Nice blue gate. Have you lived there long?
textes.traque.c4-1: Post a message to provoke him
textes.traque.o4-1: He answers publicly. Other accounts join in and your address starts going around.
textes.traque.a4-1: Your anger is legitimate. But confronting him in public can make the danger worse.
textes.traque.c4-2: Keep the evidence and make my account private
textes.traque.o4-2: You gather all the screenshots, with dates, and make your account private.
textes.traque.a4-2: A series of dated messages shows he is following you: that is strong evidence.
textes.traque.c4-3: Stop going home alone and change my routes
textes.traque.o4-3: A friend walks with you. You vary your times.
textes.traque.a4-3: Your physical safety comes before everything.
textes.traque.f4: When someone knows your address and your routes, the danger can become physical. Get someone to go with you.
textes.traque.m5-1: You blocked me? No problem. I know where to find you.
textes.traque.c5-1: Unblock him to calm him down
textes.traque.o5-1: He starts writing again, even more threatening.
textes.traque.a5-1: You did nothing wrong by blocking him. Unblocking him won't calm him down.
textes.traque.c5-2: Call the police if I feel in danger
textes.traque.o5-2: At 117, they take your situation seriously and tell you what to do.
textes.traque.a5-2: In immediate danger, call 117, day and night.
textes.traque.c5-3: File a complaint with all my screenshots
textes.traque.o5-3: You file a complaint. The National Centre for Digital Investigations can identify the account.
textes.traque.a5-3: Following and threatening someone online is punished. Dated evidence is essential.
textes.traque.f5: Harassment that follows your every step is violence. Protect your location, keep the evidence and raise the alarm.
textes.stage.m1-1: Good evening, my beautiful intern, are you asleep already?
textes.stage.c1-1: Answer with a laugh so I don't upset him
textes.stage.o1-1: He takes your answer as encouragement and writes even later the next day.
textes.stage.a1-1: You wanted to avoid a conflict with your boss, that's understandable. You can set a limit at any time.
textes.stage.c1-2: Answer the next day, staying professional
textes.stage.o1-2: “Good morning, what time is the meeting?” You bring the exchange back to work.
textes.stage.a1-2: A neutral tone and office hours set a clear limit.
textes.stage.c1-3: Take a screenshot of the message
textes.stage.o1-3: You keep the message, with the time: 11:40 pm.
textes.stage.a1-3: The time and tone of the messages are useful evidence.
textes.stage.f1: A superior has no business commenting on your appearance or writing to you at night for personal reasons.
textes.stage.m2-1: Why aren't you answering? I thought we got along well.
textes.stage.m2-2: Your evaluation also depends on your attitude, you know.
textes.stage.c2-1: Apologise and answer all his messages
textes.stage.o2-1: He gets used to writing to you every evening. You start dreading your phone.
textes.stage.a2-1: You don't have to apologise for setting limits.
textes.stage.c2-2: Tell him personal messages aren't OK with me
textes.stage.o2-2: “I'd rather our exchanges stay professional.” He doesn't answer.
textes.stage.a2-2: Saying no clearly is your right, even to a boss.
textes.stage.c2-3: Talk to my school or my tutor
textes.stage.o2-3: Your tutor listens and asks you to keep all the messages.
textes.stage.a2-3: Your school has a duty to protect you during your internship.
textes.stage.f2: Linking your evaluation to your personal “attitude” is pressure. Keep the messages and talk about it.
textes.stage.m3-1: Fill in your evaluation form here tonight, it's urgent.
textes.stage.m4-1: Come to dinner with me on Friday, we'll talk about your contract.
textes.stage.o4-1: You go reluctantly. He makes you uncomfortable all evening.
textes.stage.a4-1: You were afraid for your future, that's not a mistake. You can still talk about it and ask for help.
textes.stage.o4-2: “I'd rather we talk about it at the office.” You keep the whole conversation.
textes.stage.a4-2: A contract is discussed at the office, not over a secret dinner.
textes.stage.c4-3: Report the situation to the school and the INF
textes.stage.o4-3: Your school contacts the company. The INF explains your rights.
textes.stage.a4-3: “Nobody needs to know” is a warning sign. Talking about it protects you.
textes.stage.f4: Secrecy and power over your future are the weapons of harassment. You have the right to refuse.
textes.stage.m5-1: If you refuse again, I'll say you're incompetent.
textes.stage.c5-1: Give in to save my internship
textes.stage.o5-1: Giving in guarantees nothing and the pressure continues.
textes.stage.a5-1: Your internship is not worth your safety. You can still ask for help.
textes.stage.o5-2: With your screenshots, the school ends internships at that company and finds you another one.
textes.stage.a5-2: Dated evidence makes your word hard to dispute.
textes.stage.c5-3: File a complaint, with someone by my side
textes.stage.o5-3: The INF helps you file a complaint. The law protects women against this kind of blackmail.
textes.stage.a5-3: Demanding something from you in exchange for your work is punished by law.
textes.stage.f5: A superior who threatens your future to get something from you is committing an offence. You are not alone.
textes.fausse-connexion.m1-1: Good news! You are one of the 50 students selected for a 150,000 F grant.
textes.fausse-connexion.m1-2: To receive it, just sign in with your account. The offer expires tonight.
textes.fausse-connexion.c1-1: Great, I'll sign in right away
textes.fausse-connexion.o1-1: The account immediately sends you a link. Nobody has told you who gives this grant.
textes.fausse-connexion.a1-1: Good news makes you want to move fast: that is exactly what the trap counts on.
textes.fausse-connexion.c1-2: I didn't apply for anything: I'll check with my school
textes.fausse-connexion.o1-2: The school office doesn't know this programme. No grant is ever awarded by private message.
textes.fausse-connexion.a1-2: Checking through another channel than the message you received is the right reflex.
textes.fausse-connexion.c1-3: I ask who funds this grant
textes.fausse-connexion.o1-3: The answer: “National programme, no time to explain, the offer expires tonight.”
textes.fausse-connexion.a1-3: Urgency and vagueness are two classic signs of a scam.
textes.fausse-connexion.f1: An offer you didn't ask for, with a very short deadline, should make you slow down.
textes.fausse-connexion.m2-1: Here's the link: sign in with your account, it takes ten seconds.
textes.fausse-connexion.m3-1: To finish, you'll receive a code by SMS.
textes.fausse-connexion.m3-2: Send it to me quickly, or your place goes to another student.
textes.fausse-connexion.c3-1: Send the code so I don't lose the grant
textes.fausse-connexion.o3-1: A few minutes later you can't get into your account anymore: the password has changed.
textes.fausse-connexion.a3-1: You wanted to seize a chance. That code was the key to your account: what follows shows how to react.
textes.fausse-connexion.o3-2: The account insists, then gets angry with you. That sudden anger confirms the trap.
textes.fausse-connexion.a3-2: A code received by SMS is never shared with anyone, even for a good cause.
textes.fausse-connexion.c3-3: Change my password and turn on two-step verification
textes.fausse-connexion.o3-3: Your account is better protected: even with your password, nobody gets in without your phone.
textes.fausse-connexion.a3-3: A long password, different for every account, plus two-step verification: that's your best shield.
textes.fausse-connexion.f3: Scammers rush you so you don't have time to think. A code received by SMS is never shared.
textes.fausse-connexion.m4-1: Are you the one sending this grant link to the whole class?
textes.fausse-connexion.m4-2: Two girls clicked, and now their accounts are sending the same message.
textes.fausse-connexion.c4-1: Say nothing, I'm ashamed I fell for it
textes.fausse-connexion.o4-1: The message keeps spreading. Other students get trapped in turn.
textes.fausse-connexion.a4-1: Getting trapped is not a mistake: these traps are designed to fool everyone. Talking about it protects others.
textes.fausse-connexion.c4-2: Warn the class: don't click, it's a scam
textes.fausse-connexion.o4-2: The link stops spreading. Two friends thank you for the warning.
textes.fausse-connexion.a4-2: Warning people quickly breaks the chain.
textes.fausse-connexion.c4-3: Take my account back and sign out unknown devices
textes.fausse-connexion.o4-3: In the settings, you see an unknown device signed in. You sign it out and change your password.
textes.fausse-connexion.a4-3: Security settings show the devices signed in: check them from time to time.
textes.fausse-connexion.f4: A stolen account is used to trap the people close to you. Warning them and taking back control protects the whole group.
textes.fausse-connexion.m5-1: I got access to your photos and your conversations.
textes.fausse-connexion.m5-2: Pay 50,000 F before tomorrow, or I'll send everything to your family.
textes.fausse-connexion.o5-1: He takes the money, then asks for even more. Paying stopped nothing.
textes.fausse-connexion.a5-1: You wanted to protect yourself. Keep proof of the payment: it will help with the complaint.
textes.fausse-connexion.o5-2: He mocks you and threatens to post a first screenshot.
textes.fausse-connexion.a5-2: Anger is normal. But answering him gives him a hold on you: better to stop talking to him.
textes.fausse-connexion.c5-3: Keep the evidence, stop answering and ask for help
textes.fausse-connexion.o5-3: You take screenshots, block the account and talk to a friend, then to the CNIN.
textes.fausse-connexion.a5-3: This is the most protective reflex: evidence, blocking, reporting, support.
textes.fausse-connexion.f5: A stolen account can be used for blackmail. Don't pay, keep the evidence and get support: it is never your fault.
